chunks: Ismail ibn Qutayba said: I and Isa Shalaqan went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he initiated us by saying: How strange are those people who claim things against the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he never uttered at all! The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed the people at Kufa and said:

Praise be to God, the Inspirer of His servants to praise Him, and who created them upon the recognition of His Lordship — the One who points to His existence through His creation, and through the temporal origination of His creation to His pre-eternity, and through their mutual resemblance to each other to the fact that there is no resemblance to Him. He testifies through His signs to His power. His Essence is precluded from attributes, His being seen is precluded from eyes, and comprehending Him is precluded from imaginations.

There is no time-limit to His being and no end-point to His permanence; the senses cannot encompass Him and veils cannot cover Him — the veil between Him and His creation is His very act of creating them, due to His transcendence from what is possible in their essences, and the possibility of what is impossible for Him, and the differentiation of the Maker from the made, the Limitless from the limited, and the Lord from the governed.

The One — without the implication of a numeral; the Creator — not in the sense of movement; the All-Seeing — not by a tool; the All-Hearing — not by the separation of an organ; the Witness — not by contact; the Hidden — not by concealment; and the Manifest, the Distinct — not by the lapsing of a distance. His pre-eternity is an endpoint for the wanderings of thoughts, and His permanence is a restraint for the aspirations of intellects. His profound nature has dazzled the windows of sight, and His existence has suppressed the wanderings of imaginations.

So whoever describes God has limited Him; whoever limits Him has numbered Him; whoever numbers Him has negated His pre-eternity; whoever says 'where' has assigned Him an endpoint; whoever says 'upon what' has isolated Him; and whoever says 'in what' has contained Him.

key_terms.أَزَلُهُ: Pre-eternity, the eternal nature of God that has no beginning
key_terms.الْبَائِنُ: Distinct, separate — God is manifest yet utterly unlike creation, not distant in space but distinct in nature
key_terms.الْمَشَاعِرُ: Senses/faculties of perception — those capacities by which created beings experience the world
key_terms.الْمُمْتَنِعَةِ: Transcendent, precluded — the Essence is beyond the capacity of human description
key_terms.كُنْهُهُ: The profound true nature/depths of a thing — here, God's innermost nature which dazzles sight

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the transcendence of God in his sermon at Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam Sadiq (AS) correcting a false attribution — certain people were claiming that statements were made by Imam Ali (AS) that he never actually spoke. The Imam then cites the authentic sermon of Imam Ali (AS) delivered at Kufa, which is a masterpiece of apophatic theology (negative theology): God's Essence, vision, and comprehension are all beyond the capacity of attributes, senses, and imagination. The sermon's concluding logical chain — whoever describes/limits/numbers God has committed a theological error — was a key formulation of the Shia theological tradition, teaching that applying spatial or numerical categories to God negates His transcendence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from The Young exchanger, and his name is Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Ali Bin Sayf Bin Ameyra who said, ‘Ismail Bin Quteyba narrated to me saying, 
‘I and Isa Shalqan went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> initiated us both by saying, ‘How strange of a people claiming upon Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> what he<sup>asws</sup> never spoke with at all. Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> addressed the people at Al-Kufa, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: -

The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Inspirer of His<sup>azwj</sup> servants to Praise Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and Natured them upon the recognition of His<sup>azwj</sup> Lordship, the Indicator upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Existence by His<sup>azwj</sup> creation and by the newly occurring creation of His<sup>azwj</sup> (Indicating) upon His<sup>azwj</sup> eternality, by Making them resemble each other, that there is no resemblance for him, the testification by His<sup>azwj</sup> Signs upon His<sup>azwj</sup> Power. There are Prohibitions from describing His<sup>azwj</sup> Self, and from the sights to see Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and from the imaginations to Grasp Him<sup>azwj</sup> by it.

There is neither a time factor for Hisazwj existence nor any end-point to Hisazwj remaining. Neither can the awarenesses comprehend Himazwj nor can the veil cover Himazwj, and the veiling is between Himazwj and Hisazwj creatures. Heazwj Created them for Preventing it from what is possible in their persons and the possibility from what they are prevented from Himazwj, and for the differentiation between the Maker from the Made, and the Limitless from the limited, and the Lordazwj from the Nourished.

The One, without an explanation of a number, and the Creator, not with a prevention of movement, and the Seeing, not by tools, and the Hearing, not by a separate instrument, the Witness, not by the touching, and the Hidden, not by the covering, and the Manifest, the Remote, not by the lapsing of distance. 
His<sup>azwj</sup> eternality is an end-point for the aims of thought, and His<sup>azwj</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Permanence is a determent to the enthusiasms of the intellects. His<sup>azwj</sup> being has Blinded the windows of the sights, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Existence has Suppressed the wanderings of the imaginations.

So the one who described Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has limited Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who limits Him<sup>azwj</sup> so he has numbered Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who numbers Him<sup>azwj</sup> so he has negated His<sup>azwj</sup> eternality, and the one who says, ‘where’, so he has ascribed an end-point to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘Upon what’, so he has isolated from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘In what’, so he has contained Him<sup>azwj</sup>’’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Shabab al-Sayarafi called Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Ali ibn Sayf from ‘Amira who has said that Isma‘il ibn Qutayba said the following. “I and ‘Isa ibn al-Shalqan went to see Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.). The Imam said ‘It is strange that a group of people ascribe to Amirul Mu’minin certain things that he had never said. Amirul Mu’minin addressed people in Kufa in the following words. “

All praise is due to Allah Who inspired His servants with His praise and natured them in a way that would give them the desire to acknowledge His Lordship. It is He, Who guides people through His creation to His Own existence and His creatures are evidence of His eternity. The fact that His creatures are similar is evidence that there is nothing similar to Him. His signs are evidence of His great power. His Own-self prohibits acceptance of descriptions and so are His being seen with the eyes and His being comprehended in the imaginations.

There is no time limit for His being in existence and there is no final destination for Him. Awareness can not contain Him and coverings can not cover Him. The curtain between Him and His creatures is His creating them. It is because of being impossible for Him what is possible in the essence of the creatures and because of what may be possible in their case is impossible in His case. It is also because of the difference between the Creator and the created, the limited and the unlimited and the Lord and the worshippers.

He is One without being a unit of a particular kind. He is the Creator but not terms of motion. He is seeing but not by means of tools. He is hearing but not with distinguishing instruments. He observes but not by means of touching. He is hidden but not with covering. He is clearly manifest but not with lapse due to distance. His eternity is beyond the reach of thinking and a stop for the aims of the intelligence. His reality has worn out the ability of sight and His Own-self has uprooted the (spreading) vines of imaginations.

Whoever tries to describe Allah has thought of Him as limited and whoever considers Him limited he has enumerated Him and whoever enumerates Him he has invalidated His eternity. Whoever asks where is He, he has considered Him as having an end. Whoever says on what is He, he has considered Him as distanced. Whoever says wherein is He, he has considered Him contained in some thing.”
